bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw Material & Resource Security — Rated High impact: fluctuations in mineral availability, mining regulations, energy costs and logistics expenses may impact production costs and margins; mitigated via diversified/planned sourcing, captive mining reserves, strategic inventory management and long-term supplier partnerships.
- Demand Cyclicality Across End-Use Industries — Rated Medium impact: a slowdown in paints, polymers, rubber, ceramics or construction sectors could affect volumes and profitability; mitigated via a diversified end-market portfolio, expansion into specialty applications and customer diversification.
- Global Trade, Export & Geopolitical Risk — Rated Medium impact: trade restrictions, freight disruptions, currency volatility and geopolitical developments may affect export competitiveness and supply chains; mitigated via a balanced domestic-export mix, market diversification and active treasury management.
- Operational & Project Execution Risk — Rated Medium impact: delays in capacity expansion, integration of overseas assets, or operational disruptions may impact growth objectives; mitigated via structured project governance and performance monitoring systems.
- Sustainability, Environmental & Regulatory Risk — Rated High impact: increasing environmental regulations, ESG expectations and compliance requirements may affect operating costs and market access; mitigated via ISO/Responsible Care practices and regular environmental audits.
- Technology, Cybersecurity & Digital Risk — Rated Medium impact: increased digitalisation exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; mitigated via strengthened IT governance, cybersecurity protocols and disaster recovery systems.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as "India's largest producer of micronized minerals" and, in the CMD profile, as "India's largest producer of micronized industrial minerals and specialty chemicals, with a presence in over 65 countries".
- Self-described as "the pioneers in the field of Industrial Minerals in India", built on "expertise in Micronization", now "expanding our portfolio into the world of Performance Minerals, Speciality Chemicals and Functional Additives catering to the niche segments".
- R&D moat framed around a "devoted R&D and Product Application Centre"; the state-of-the-art R&D Centre at Waghodia, Vadodara is "recognized and approved by DSIR, Govt. of India".
- Management frames the strategic backdrop around the global 'China plus one' strategy, "positioning the company as a reliable global player", and cites "import substitution capabilities" as an expected benefit of the capex.
- Group structure spans subsidiaries (20 Microns Nano, 20 Microns Malaysia, 20 Microns FZE Sharjah, 20 MCC, IQ Marbles, GTLQ, 20 Microns Vietnam) and German JVs (Dorfner 20 Microns for coloured quartz; Sievert 20 Microns Building Materials for tile adhesives and construction chemicals).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] "Expanded its global presence by entering into definitive agreements to acquire 100% equity interest in GTLQ SDN BHD and IQ Marbles SDN BHD, a well-established limestone extraction and processing businesses based in Ipoh, Malaysia"; both appear in the group structure as Malaysian limestone reserves and processing.
- [JV] "Entered into JV Agreement with Sievert Baustoff GmbH, Germany for Manufacturing of Construction Chemicals", with a "new joint venture company incorporated as Sievert 20 Microns Building Materials Private Limited for construction chemicals and building related products".
- [JV] Entered into a JV agreement with Dorfner "to further strengthen 20ML's international presence"; Dorfner 20 Microns is described as a German JV supplying Coloured Quartz.
- [Demand backdrop] Management flags FY26 headwinds: "subdued paint industry demand, prolonged monsoon impact on post-Diwali offtake, and geopolitical uncertainties arising from the West Asia conflict".
- [Outreach] Exhibited at PlastIndia 2026 (New Delhi, 5-10 Feb 2026) showing functional fillers, anti-blocking agents and specialty additives for polymers, and at PaintIndia 2026 (Mumbai, 19-21 Feb 2026) showing engineered nanoparticle-based inorganic additives.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: 20 Microns Limited mines, beneficiates and micronizes industrial minerals (talc, kaolin, calcite, dolomite, silica) and processes them into specialty minerals, functional additives, construction chemicals and agriculture (MinFert) products for customers in paints and coatings, plastics and polymers, specialty chemicals, rubber, construction and agriculture. The Company sells over 50 specialty products domestically and through an international business serving export markets, supported by subsidiaries and joint ventures in minerals processing and building materials.

- **Innovation-led Products:** TALC HFM 25 SD, White Kaolin Cosmetic Grade, HYPERTHERM UT, HYDROXYLGEL A1
- **Agriculture (MinFert Division):** MinFert BLK Series, MinFert GBR Series, MinFert Humicrons, MinFert Geo Care, Thalaivaa

outlook.body: Diversification into specialty materials and additives, expansion into construction chemicals and exports
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Structural shift from an industrial-minerals foundation toward a more specialised, innovation-led portfolio focused on advanced materials and speciality applications
- Accelerating growth of speciality and high-performance materials
- Scaling up emerging verticals such as the fertilizer (MinFert) and construction chemicals divisions
- Expanding global footprint with a sharper focus on value-added, speciality export products and customer-specific solutions
- Strengthening operational efficiency through technology and process/IT-digital integration
- Maintaining a disciplined focus on capital allocation
- Deepening technical capabilities, customer engagement and a solutions-oriented approach to product development, moving the business from mineral supply toward application partnership
- Continued investment in long-term capabilities via capacity expansions, backward integration initiatives, and a calibrated approach to entering new geographies
- Vision to be the global Minerals & Specialty Chemical industry benchmark for value creation and corporate citizenship
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's three-year strategic roadmap is anchored in six growth pillars backed by a Rs.100 crore capex investment plan to be deployed over 24 months: (1) Capacity Expansion - upgrading infra-tech across existing and planned manufacturing/R&D facilities and strengthening quarrying for captive consumption; (2) Product Innovation - launching new variants across 4 breakthrough platforms and developing nano-mineral, bio-surface modifier and EV-battery mineral applications; (3) Export Acceleration - customer qualification in the EU, US, Middle East and ASEAN, leveraging 2-Star Export House status, with cosmetic-grade kaolin and HYPERTHERM UT positioned as near-term export anchors; (4) Strategic Partnerships & Acquisitions - the Sievert 20 Microns JV targeting a production ramp to 22,500 MTPA by FY29, and the Malaysian subsidiary targeting quarrying capacity of 92,000 MTPA and processing capacity of 1,08,000 MTPA by FY30; (5) Digital Transformation - rollout of an AI-powered CRM (20MCRM), vendor bank validation, GST verification and advanced EHS reporting; and (6) Sustainability & ESG - 15% of the capex plan directed to energy optimisation, waste reduction and green manufacturing, targeting a 15% reduction in carbon emissions over 3 years and 5-8% energy cost savings. Separately, per the CEO's message, the Company is securing backward integration through strategic mining acquisitions including its entry into Malaysian resources, with further expansions underway, and operates two R&D and product-application centres in Vadodara that are being aligned with future-facing sectors such as renewable energy and semiconductors.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India sustained strong economic momentum in FY26 (Economic Survey 2025-26 projecting real GDP growth of ~7.3-7.4%), driven by robust domestic demand, expanding services/industry activity and resilient investment trends, with manufacturing GVA outpacing the broader industrial sector
- India's mining sector showed robust momentum in FY26, with the National Critical Mineral Mission and infrastructure-led demand seen as structurally positive for industrial mineral producers
- Across end-use industries, three structural shifts are benefiting the Company's positioning: customers moving from volume to value (performance-enhanced, specification-driven inputs), from cost to optimisation (yield/formulation efficiency, supply reliability), and from compliance to competitiveness (sustainability, traceability); the Company's mineral-based solutions are increasingly positioned in higher-value applications rather than commoditised supply chains
- India's paints and coatings industry is projected to grow at roughly 6.5% CAGR to 2030, supported by automotive, construction and infrastructure expansion, urbanisation and rising disposable income - a key demand driver for the Company's mineral inputs
- While certain legacy segments experienced moderated demand, the Company maintained consistent margins and continued to strengthen its positioning in higher-value segments
- The 20MCC Fertilizer Division continues to gain traction, supported by increasing awareness around soil health and sustainable agricultural practices
- The Construction Chemicals Division delivered encouraging growth, benefiting from strong momentum in infrastructure and real estate development and an expanding application footprint
- International business remained resilient despite geopolitical disruptions and logistical challenges, with continued deepening of presence across key export markets and a sharper focus on speciality products and customer-specific solutions
- FY27 macro outlook is viewed as positive but adjustment-oriented, with global trade uncertainty and tariff pressures on exporters expected to ease as domestic demand and investment strengthen
